diagram_math_checks.result: G has V={x,y,w,c,t} and exactly x->w, y->w, w->c, w->t. It is finite and acyclic, ordered x,y before w before c,t. X={x}, Y={y}, C={c} are pairwise disjoint. These instantiate def-d-separation-in-a-dag and the lemma Statement.
Using def-ancestral-moral-graph-of-a-dag, H=An_G({x,y,c})={x,y,w,c}: w reaches c; t has no outgoing arrow and reaches none of x,y,c. Thus G[H] retains exactly x->w, y->w, w->c, as drawn in panel 2.

On path x,w,y the only internal vertex w receives both arrows and has descendant c in C. F1 therefore makes the path active. Step 1.1 replaces x->w<-y by the moral x-y edge; conversely step 1.2 may expand that edge using common child w. No broader route or splicing assertion is inferred from the example.

By F2 and the exact local moral-graph definition, panel 3 has skeleton edges x-w, y-w, w-c and one added edge x-y, since x,y are the only distinct parents of a common child. Its four vertices have degrees x=2,y=2,w=3,c=1. Every segment is explicit; no cycle closure shorthand is used.

Deleting C={c} removes c and only its edge w-c. Panel 4 has vertices x,y,w and exactly edges x-w,y-w,x-y, all degree 2. The direct x-y edge survives, so no undirected separation holds, agreeing with the active DAG path and the lemma equivalence.

Within DAG panels arrowheads encode precisely the declared directions. Moral panels are undirected; dashed x-y marks only the newly added ordinary edge, not a special edge type. Three between-panel arrows denote graph operations, not DAG edges or category morphisms. The rigorous numbered proof is unchanged and independent of the illustration.
